bull.b: The long-dated Rockdale lease adds substantial contracted revenue beyond Bitcoin mining and supports a more infrastructure-like business model. Its high illustrative NOI margin and phased delivery could improve revenue visibility and diversification as capacity is brought online.

Low power costs are a durable competitive advantage in Bitcoin mining, where electricity is a core operating input. Maintaining this efficiency can protect mining economics, support production through difficult network conditions, and improve Riot’s ability to scale capacity.

Growth in the engineering segment, expanding margins, and a substantial data-center-focused backlog demonstrate useful internal execution capabilities. Increased manufacturing capacity may help Riot deliver contracted projects on schedule and reduce dependence on external infrastructure delivery.

bear.b: Persistent losses and negative cash generation weaken internal funding capacity and reduce financial resilience. Unless profitability improves, Riot may need to keep selling assets, raising capital, or using debt to support operations and its expansion program, increasing execution pressure.

The data-center opportunity requires very large upfront investment before the contracted economics are fully realized. Heavy capital needs and planned borrowing increase execution, financing, and construction risk, while delays could postpone revenue and extend the period of cash consumption.

Bitcoin mining remains a major earnings driver, leaving financial performance exposed to variables Riot cannot control. Changes in Bitcoin economics or network competition can compress margins quickly, while the company’s sale of mined Bitcoin to fund development reduces treasury exposure but adds funding dependence.
